claim: RLCM's reward widens the margin between confidence assigned at correct vs. incorrect intermediate reasoning steps within a single trajectory (process-level, margin-enhanced), rather than pushing confidence toward the empirical accuracy rate as calibration-only rewards do.
stance_target: discrimination (margin/ranking) is a distinct training target from calibration (accuracy-matching)
scope_conditions: process-level reward design over intermediate-budget completions
quoted_support: Rather than aligning confidence to correctness likelihoods, RLCM encourages to widen the confidence margin between correct and incorrect steps within a single reasoning trajectory.

claim: RLCM reads confidence out via a lightweight linear probe trained on hidden states at forced-completion checkpoints, not via a verbalized confidence token generated by the model -- explicitly separate from the natural-language interface a user reads.
stance_target: state-of-the-art calibration-aware RL produces an EXPRESSED (user-visible) confidence interface
quoted_support: Prior work shows that LLM hidden states encode useful signals about the model's internal confidence, which can be extracted with lightweight probes.

claim: Despite training only on math (GRPO-LEAD), RLCM generalizes out-of-domain to LiveCodeBench (code), achieving the best accuracy AND the best calibration among all compared methods on that benchmark, alongside best results on GPQA (science).
stance_target: calibration-aware RL trained on math can transfer to code without code-specific training data
quoted_support: Although all methods are trained on math-centric data, RLCM remains strong on coding, science, and logical reasoning tasks. It achieves the best accuracy on LiveCodeBench and GPQA while also attaining the best calibration on those datasets.

claim: RLCM's own baseline comparison shows verbalized confidence (RLCR) and logit-based confidence (C2GSPG) UNDERPERFORM a hidden-state linear probe on both accuracy and calibration error, with the verbalized/logit signals occupying a 'much narrower range,' making them less expressive.
stance_target: verbalized confidence interfaces can match internal-signal discrimination quality
scope_conditions: math in-domain and OOD (science, code, logic) benchmarks, R1-distilled-Qwen-7B
quoted_support: Verbalized and logit-based confidence are insufficient. Although RLCR (verbalized confidence) and C2GSPG (logit-based confidence) are both designed to improve calibration, they underperform GRPO not only in accuracy but also in PCE and ECE... their confidence signals occupy a much narrower range than RLCM's probe-based confidence, making them less expressive and more poorly calibrated.

claim: RLCM was trained on a single 4xH100 NVL node with batch size 32, 6 rollouts per prompt, learning rate 1e-6, over ~2.5 epochs (600 update steps), using the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B base model.
quoted_support: All methods are trained with a batch size of 32, learning rate 10^-6, 6 rollouts, temperature 0.8, 8k maximum generation tokens, and 600 update steps (~2.5 epochs)... All experiments are conducted on a single 4xH100 NVL node.

claim: RLCM's calibrated confidence enables more efficient conformal risk control and effective confidence-weighted aggregation across token budgets, showing discriminative process-level confidence has direct downstream utility for test-time compute allocation.
stance_target: discriminative confidence signals have practical value for inference-time control
scope_conditions: confidence-weighted aggregation and conformal risk control experiments
quoted_support: We further show that, with calibrated confidence signals, the resulting models enable more efficient conformal risk control and effective confidence-weighted aggregation.
